claim: Cilia defects lead to scoliosis in zebrafish.
source: Cilia defects lead to scoliosis in zebrafish, but the underlying pathogenic mechanisms are poorly understood and may diverge depending on the mutated gene.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge in the field.

claim: rpgrip1l mutant fish developed scoliosis with near-total penetrance but asynchronous onset in juveniles.
source: rpgrip1l mutant fish developed scoliosis with near-total penetrance but asynchronous onset in juveniles.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Curvature onset was preceded by ventricle dilations in rpgrip1l mutants.
source: Taking advantage of this asynchrony, we found that curvature onset was preceded by ventricle dilations and was concomitant to the perturbation of Reissner fiber polymerization and to the loss of multiciliated tufts around the subcommissural organ.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Curvature onset was concomitant to the perturbation of Reissner fiber polymerization in rpgrip1l mutants.
source: Taking advantage of this asynchrony, we found that curvature onset was preceded by ventricle dilations and was concomitant to the perturbation of Reissner fiber polymerization and to the loss of multiciliated tufts around the subcommissural organ.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Curvature onset was concomitant to the loss of multiciliated tufts around the subcommissural organ in rpgrip1l mutants.
source: Taking advantage of this asynchrony, we found that curvature onset was preceded by ventricle dilations and was concomitant to the perturbation of Reissner fiber polymerization and to the loss of multiciliated tufts around the subcommissural organ.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: Rpgrip1l is exclusively required in foxj1a-expressing cells to prevent axis curvature.
source: Rescue experiments showed that Rpgrip1l was exclusively required in foxj1a-expressing cells to prevent axis curvature.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by rescue experiment data in Figure 1.

claim: Urp1/2 levels are not a main driver of scoliosis in rpgrip1 mutants.
source: Genetic interactions investigations ruled out Urp1/2 levels as a main driver of scoliosis in rpgrip1 mutants.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by genetic interaction data in Figure 4.

claim: Neuroinflammation associated with increased Annexin levels is a potential mechanism of scoliosis development in rpgrip1l juveniles.
source: Transcriptomic and proteomic studies identified neuroinflammation associated with increased Annexin levels as a potential mechanism of scoliosis development in rpgrip1l juveniles.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by transcriptomic and proteomic data in Figure 5.

claim: Astrogliosis arises in glial cells surrounding the diencephalic and rhombencephalic ventricles just before scoliosis onset in rpgrip1l mutants.
source: Investigating the cell types associated with annexin2 over-expression, we uncovered astrogliosis, arising in glial cells surrounding the diencephalic and rhombencephalic ventricles just before scoliosis onset and increasing with time in severity.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by immunostaining data in Figure 6.

claim: Astrogliosis increases with time in severity in rpgrip1l mutants.
source: Investigating the cell types associated with annexin2 over-expression, we uncovered astrogliosis, arising in glial cells surrounding the diencephalic and rhombencephalic ventricles just before scoliosis onset and increasing with time in severity.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by immunostaining data in Figure 6.

claim: Anti-inflammatory drug treatment reduced scoliosis penetrance and severity in rpgrip1l mutants.
source: Anti-inflammatory drug treatment reduced scoliosis penetrance and severity and this correlated with reduced astrogliosis and macrophage/microglia enrichment around the diencephalic ventricle.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by NACET treatment data in Figure 7.

claim: Anti-inflammatory drug treatment correlated with reduced astrogliosis in rpgrip1l mutants.
source: Anti-inflammatory drug treatment reduced scoliosis penetrance and severity and this correlated with reduced astrogliosis and macrophage/microglia enrichment around the diencephalic ventricle.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by NACET treatment data in Figure 7.

claim: Anti-inflammatory drug treatment correlated with reduced macrophage/microglia enrichment around the diencephalic ventricle in rpgrip1l mutants.
source: Anti-inflammatory drug treatment reduced scoliosis penetrance and severity and this correlated with reduced astrogliosis and macrophage/microglia enrichment around the diencephalic ventricle.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by NACET treatment data in Figure 7.

claim: Mutation of the cep290 gene encoding another transition zone protein associates astrogliosis with scoliosis.
source: Mutation of the cep290 gene encoding another transition zone protein also associated astrogliosis with scoliosis.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by immunostaining data in Figure 8.

claim: Astrogliosis induced by perturbed ventricular homeostasis and associated with immune cell activation is a novel pathogenic mechanism of zebrafish scoliosis caused by cilia dysfunction.
source: Thus, we propose astrogliosis induced by perturbed ventricular homeostasis and associated with immune cell activation as a novel pathogenic mechanism of zebrafish scoliosis caused by cilia dysfunction.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, based on the integration of multiple experimental findings.

claim: Idiopathic scoliosis affects about 3% of adolescents worldwide.
source: Idiopathic scoliosis (IS) is a 3D rotation of the spine without vertebral anomalies that affects about 3% of adolescents worldwide.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The etiology of idiopathic scoliosis remained mysterious mainly because of the lack of appropriate animal models and the complexity of its inheritance profile.
source: Its etiology remained mysterious, mainly because of the lack of appropriate animal models and the complexity of its inheritance profile in large families presenting a severe scoliosis trait (Patten et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by a citation.

claim: The zebrafish ptk7 gene mutant was the first IS model described.
source: Since the description of the first IS model in the zebrafish ptk7 gene mutant (Hayes et al., 2014), a number of mutants for genes encoding ciliary proteins were shown to develop scoliosis at late larval and juvenile stage (4–12 weeks post-fertilization, wpf) without any vertebral fusion or fracture, highlighting the link between cilia function and straight axis maintenance in that species (Grimes et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by a citation.

claim: A number of mutants for genes encoding ciliary proteins develop scoliosis at late larval and juvenile stage (4–12 weeks post-fertilization, wpf) without any vertebral fusion or fracture.
source: Since the description of the first IS model in the zebrafish ptk7 gene mutant (Hayes et al., 2014), a number of mutants for genes encoding ciliary proteins were shown to develop scoliosis at late larval and juvenile stage (4–12 weeks post-fertilization, wpf) without any vertebral fusion or fracture, highlighting the link between cilia function and straight axis maintenance in that species (Grimes et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by citations.

claim: There is a link between cilia function and straight axis maintenance in zebrafish.
source: Since the description of the first IS model in the zebrafish ptk7 gene mutant (Hayes et al., 2014), a number of mutants for genes encoding ciliary proteins were shown to develop scoliosis at late larval and juvenile stage (4–12 weeks post-fertilization, wpf) without any vertebral fusion or fracture, highlighting the link between cilia function and straight axis maintenance in that species (Grimes et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by citations.

claim: Zebrafish mutants in genes involved in cilia motility or in intraflagellar transport display severe embryonic axis curvature and are usually not viable beyond larval stages.
source: Zebrafish mutants in genes involved in cilia motility or in intraflagellar transport display severe embryonic axis curvature and are usually not viable beyond larval stages (Grimes et al., 2016; Rose et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by citations.

claim: Mutants in genes implicated in ciliary gating or ciliary trafficking encoding respectively components of the transition zone (TZ) or of the BBsome complex survive to adult stage and develop scoliosis with variable penetrance.
source: In contrast, mutants in genes implicated in ciliary gating or ciliary trafficking encoding respectively components of the transition zone (TZ) or of the BBsome complex survive to adult stage and develop scoliosis with variable penetrance (Bentley-Ford et al., 2022; Masek et al., 2022; Song et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by citations.

claim: Cilia-driven movements of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) are involved in zebrafish axis straightness, both in embryos and juveniles.
source: Cilia-driven movements of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) are involved in zebrafish axis straightness, both in embryos and juveniles (Boswell and Ciruna, 2017; Grimes et al., 2016) and are tightly linked to the assembly and maintenance of the Reissner fiber (RF), a SCO-spondin polymer secreted by the subcommissural organ (SCO) and running down the brain and spinal cord CSF-filled cavities (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by citations.

claim: Cilia-driven movements of the cerebrospinal fluid are tightly linked to the assembly and maintenance of the Reissner fiber (RF).
source: Cilia-driven movements of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) are involved in zebrafish axis straightness, both in embryos and juveniles (Boswell and Ciruna, 2017; Grimes et al., 2016) and are tightly linked to the assembly and maintenance of the Reissner fiber (RF), a SCO-spondin polymer secreted by the subcommissural organ (SCO) and running down the brain and spinal cord CSF-filled cavities (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by a citation.

claim: The Reissner fiber is a SCO-spondin polymer secreted by the subcommissural organ (SCO) and running down the brain and spinal cord CSF-filled cavities.
source: Cilia-driven movements of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) are involved in zebrafish axis straightness, both in embryos and juveniles (Boswell and Ciruna, 2017; Grimes et al., 2016) and are tightly linked to the assembly and maintenance of the Reissner fiber (RF), a SCO-spondin polymer secreted by the subcommissural organ (SCO) and running down the brain and spinal cord CSF-filled cavities (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by a citation.

claim: RF loss at embryonic stage in null sspo mutants generates ventral curvatures of the posterior axis of the body and is lethal.
source: RF loss at embryonic stage in null sspo mutants generates ventral curvatures of the posterior axis of the body and is lethal while its loss at juvenile stage in hypomorphic sspo mutants triggers scoliosis with full penetrance (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018; Rose et al., 2020; Troutwine et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by citations.

claim: RF loss at juvenile stage in hypomorphic sspo mutants triggers scoliosis with full penetrance.
source: RF loss at embryonic stage in null sspo mutants generates ventral curvatures of the posterior axis of the body and is lethal while its loss at juvenile stage in hypomorphic sspo mutants triggers scoliosis with full penetrance (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018; Rose et al., 2020; Troutwine et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by citations.

claim: Signaling downstream of the RF in embryos implicates Urp1 and Urp2, two neuropeptides of the Urotensin 2 family expressed in ventral CSF-contacting neurons (CSF-cNs), which act on dorsal muscles in embryos and larvae.
source: Signaling downstream of the RF in embryos implicates Urp1 and Urp2, two neuropeptides of the Urotensin 2 family expressed in ventral CSF-contacting neurons (CSF-cNs), which act on dorsal muscles in embryos and larvae (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2020; Gaillard et al., 2023; Lu et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by citations.

claim: Combined mutations of urp1 and urp2 or the mutation of their receptor gene uts2r3 lead to scoliosis at adult stages.
source: Their combined mutations or the mutation of their receptor gene uts2r3 lead to scoliosis at adult stages (Bearce et al., 2022; Gaillard et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by citations.

claim: Two scoliotic models develop axial curvature while maintaining a RF showing that their curvature onset occurs independently of RF loss.
source: Moreover, two scoliotic models develop axial curvature while maintaining a RF showing that their curvature onset occurs independently of RF loss (Meyer-Miner et al., 2022; Xie et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by citations.

claim: Neuro-inflammation has been described in a small subset of zebrafish IS models for which anti-inflammatory/anti-oxidant treatments (with NAC or NACET) partially rescue scoliosis penetrance and severity.
source: Finally, neuro-inflammation has been described in a small subset of zebrafish IS models for which anti-inflammatory/anti-oxidant treatments (with NAC or NACET) partially rescue scoliosis penetrance and severity (Rose et al., 2020; Van Gennip et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by citations.

claim: RPGRIP1L mutations have been found in neurodevelopmental ciliopathies, Meckel syndrome (MKS) and Joubert syndrome (JS) characterized by severe brain malformations.
source: RPGRIP1L mutations have been found in neurodevelopmental ciliopathies, Meckel syndrome (MKS) and Joubert syndrome (JS; Delous et al., 2007; Arts et al., 2007) characterized by severe brain malformations.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by citations.

claim: Some JS patients present with severe scoliosis, but this phenotypic trait is of variable penetrance.
source: Some JS patients also present with severe scoliosis, but this phenotypic trait is of variable penetrance (Delous et al., 2007; Brancati et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by citations.

claim: Rpgrip1l is required for proper central nervous system patterning due to complex perturbations of Sonic Hedgehog signaling (in mice) and cilia planar positioning (in mice and zebrafish).
source: Functional studies performed in mouse and zebrafish have shown that Rpgrip1l is required for proper central nervous system patterning due to complex perturbations of Sonic Hedgehog signaling (in mice) and cilia planar positioning (in mice and zebrafish; Andreu-Cervera et al., 2021; Mahuzier et al., 2012; Vierkotten et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, supported by citations.

claim: 90–100% of rpgrip1l∆/∆ embryos and larvae were straight (0–10%, depending on the clutch, displayed a sigmoid curvature).
source: 90–100% of rpgrip1l∆/∆ embryos and larvae were straight (0–10%, depending on the clutch, displayed a sigmoid curvature).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section.

claim: rpgrip1l∆/∆ embryos did not display any additional defects found in many ciliary mutant embryos or larvae such as randomized left-right asymmetry, kidney cysts, or retinal anomalies.
source: They did not display any additional defects found in many ciliary mutant embryos or larvae such as randomized left-right asymmetry, kidney cysts, or retinal anomalies (Bachmann-Gagescu et al., 2011; Kramer-Zucker et al., 2005; Tsujikawa and Malicki, 2004; Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, D, E).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: rpgrip1l-/- animals developed scoliosis during juvenile stages.
source: rpgrip1l-/- animals developed scoliosis during juvenile stages.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section.

claim: Scoliosis appearance was asynchronous between clutches, from 4 weeks post fertilization (wpf) (around 1 cm length) to 11 wpf (1,8–2,3 cm), and also within a clutch.
source: Scoliosis appearance was asynchronous between clutches, from 4 weeks post fertilization (wpf) (around 1 cm length) to 11 wpf (1,8–2,3 cm), and also within a clutch.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section.

claim: Scoliosis started with slight upward bending of the tail (the tail-up phenotype) and progressed toward severe curvature with 90% penetrance in adults (100% in females and 80% in males).
source: It started with slight upward bending of the tail (the tail-up phenotype) and progressed toward severe curvature (Figure 1A and B) with 90% penetrance in adults (100% in females and 80% in males; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Micro-computed tomography (μCT) confirmed that spine curvature was three-dimensional and showed no evidence of vertebral fusion, malformation, or fracture.
source: Micro-computed tomography (μCT) at two different stages (5 wpf and 23 wpf) confirmed that spine curvature was three-dimensional and showed no evidence of vertebral fusion, malformation, or fracture (Figure 1D–G and Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: The Foxj1a:5XMycRPGRIP1L transgene was sufficient to fully suppress scoliosis in rpgrip1l-/- fish.
source: The Foxj1a:5XMycRPGRIP1L transgene was sufficient to fully suppress scoliosis in rpgrip1l-/- fish: none of the transgenic rpgrip1l-/- fish became scoliotic while virtually all the non-transgenic rpgrip1l-/- siblings did (Figure 1I and J).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: RPGRIP1L expression triggered by the col2a1a promoter did not have any beneficial effect on scoliosis penetrance.
source: In contrast, RPGRIP1L expression triggered by the col2a1a promoter did not have any beneficial effect on scoliosis penetrance (Figure 1I and J).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: rpgrip1l expression in foxj1a-expressing cells is sufficient to maintain a straight axis.
source: In conclusion, rpgrip1l expression in foxj1a-expressing cells is sufficient to maintain a straight axis.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on rescue experiment data.

claim: In 3-month adults, cilia tufts of multiciliated ependymal cells (MCC) lining the ventricle were present in controls and straight rpgrip1l-/- fish.
source: In 3-month adults, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) at the level of the rhombencephalic ventricle (RhV) showed cilia tufts of multiciliated ependymal cells (MCC) lining the ventricle in controls and straight rpgrip1l-/- fish (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–G, F'-G').
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: In scoliotic rpgrip1l-/- fish, cilia tufts were sparse and disorganized.
source: In scoliotic rpgrip1l-/- fish, cilia tufts were sparse and disorganized (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H, H').
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: In the spinal cord central canal of 8 wpf juvenile fish, cilia density was reduced to the same extent in rpgrip1l-/- fish irrespective of the fish curvature status.
source: In the spinal cord central canal of 8 wpf juvenile fish, cilia density was reduced to the same extent in rpgrip1l-/- fish irrespective of the fish curvature status (Figure 2A–C and E).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Cilia length increased in straight mutants and was more heterogenous than controls in scoliotic mutants.
source: In addition, cilia length increased in straight mutants and was more heterogenous than controls in scoliotic mutants (Figure 2A'–C' and D).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Arl13b content appeared severely reduced in mutants.
source: Arl13b content appeared severely reduced in mutants (Figure 2A"–C").
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: rpgrip1l-/- juveniles presented an incomplete penetrance of ciliary defects in the fChP, with no correlation between cilia defects and the curvature status.
source: rpgrip1l-/- juveniles presented an incomplete penetrance of ciliary defects in the fChP, with no correlation between cilia defects and the curvature status (Figure 2—figure supplement 1L–O'').
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Monocilia of Sspo secreting cells were still present but appeared longer in straight rpgrip1l-/- juveniles and could not be individualized anymore at anterior SCO level in scoliotic fish.
source: Monocilia of Sspo secreting cells were still present but appeared longer in straight rpgrip1l-/- juveniles and could not be individualized anymore at anterior SCO level in scoliotic fish: we observed a weaker and denser acetylated and glutamylated tubulin staining that likely corresponded to longer intertwined cilia (Figure 2I, I', K and K').
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Lateral multicilia tufts were preserved in straight rpgrip1l-/- juveniles but were missing at posterior SCO level in tail-up or scoliotic rpgrip1l-/- fish.
source: Lateral multicilia tufts were preserved in straight rpgrip1l-/- juveniles (n=5) (Figure 2J) but were missing at posterior SCO level in tail-up or scoliotic rpgrip1l-/- fish (n=7) (Figure 2L).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: The loss of MCC cilia at the SCO strictly correlates with scoliosis onset.
source: By contrast, the loss of MCC cilia at the SCO strictly correlates with scoliosis onset, suggesting a causal relationship.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on correlation data.

claim: The lumen of the central canal was enlarged at thoracic and lumbar levels in all rpgrip1l-/- mutant juveniles, with no correlation to the axis curvature status.
source: In the spinal cord, the lumen of the central canal was enlarged at thoracic and lumbar levels in all rpgrip1l-/- mutant juveniles, with no correlation to the axis curvature status (Figure 2A–C, F).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: A significant increase in ventricle volume in rpgrip1l-/- fish compared to controls was identified, restricted to the ventral regions of the RhV in regions ROI4.4 and ROI6.
source: We identified a significant increase in ventricle volume in rpgrip1l-/- fish compared to controls, that was restricted to the ventral regions of the RhV in regions ROI4.4 (green sphere in Figure 3C) and ROI6 (green sphere in Figure 3D), as confirmed by numerical sections (Figure 3E and G).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: The RF was present in all controls and in all rpgrip1l-/- straight fish.
source: The RF was visualized as a 1 μm diameter rod in the central canal of the neural tube and few dots were present in the apical cytoplasm of FP cells (Figure 3I) as well as in the SCO of all controls (n=8, Figure 3L and O) and in ventricles caudal to the SCO (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H). The RF was also present in all rpgrip1l-/- straight fish (n=9, Figure 3J, Figure 2—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: In rpgrip1l-/- tail-up and scoliotic fish, the RF was absent at all axis levels and a few SCO-spondin-positive debris were present in the central canal.
source: In contrast, in rpgrip1l-/- tail-up and scoliotic fish, the RF was absent at all axis levels and a few SCO-spondin-positive debris were present in the central canal (n=8, Figure 3K).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Transverse sections at the level of the SCO and caudal to the SCO in severely scoliotic fish revealed abnormally packed material in the ventricle.
source: Transverse sections at the level of the SCO and caudal to the SCO in severely scoliotic fish revealed abnormally packed material in the ventricle (Figure 3N and Q, Figure 2—figure supplement 1J), while Sspo secreted cells from rpgrip1l-/- at scoliosis onset, that is in juveniles with a slight tail-up phenotype, appeared to produce Sspo-GFP cytoplasmic granules as in controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, B', D).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Sspo aggregates spread anteriorly into the diencephalic ventricle (DiV) at fChP level in scoliotic juveniles.
source: We also observed that Sspo aggregates spread anteriorly into the diencephalic ventricle (DiV) at fChP level in scoliotic juveniles (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G, n=7/7), a situation never observed in controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E, n=0/6) or in straight juveniles (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F, n=0/5).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: There is a strict temporal correlation between the loss of MCC at posterior SCO level, impaired RF polymerization and scoliosis onset in rpgrip1l-/- juvenile fish.
source: Thus, our study uncovers a strict temporal correlation between the loss of MCC at posterior SCO level, impaired RF polymerization and scoliosis onset in rpgrip1l-/- juvenile fish.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on correlation data.

claim: urp2 was the most highly expressed gene among all urotensin 2 members at juvenile stage.
source: urp2 was the most highly expressed gene among all urotensin 2 members at juvenile stage (Figure 4A, D and E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–E).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: urp2 expression was upregulated in 5 weeks juveniles, both in straight and scoliotic fish and its upregulation was maintained in adult scoliotic fish.
source: urp2 expression was upregulated in 5 weeks juveniles, both in straight and scoliotic fish and its upregulation was maintained in adult scoliotic fish (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: The removal of one or two urp2 functional allele(s) in rpgrip1l-/- fish did not lower their curvature index.
source: Using a curvature quantification method on whole fish (Figure 4—figure supplement 1I and Materials and methods), we observed that the removal of one or two urp2 functional allele(s) in rpgrip1l-/- fish did not lower their curvature index (Figure 4B), neither at two mpf (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F) nor at four mpf (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G–H).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Lowering global Urp1/2 expression level in rpgrip1l mutants did not have any beneficial effect on the axis curvature phenotype.
source: Thus, lowering global Urp1/2 expression level in rpgrip1l mutants did not have any beneficial effect on the axis curvature phenotype, ruling out altered urp1/2 signaling as a main driver of scoliosis in rpgrip1l mutants.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on genetic interaction data.

claim: Differential gene expression (DGE) analysis recovered a vast majority of upregulated genes in the dorsal trunk (75 downregulated vs 614 upregulated genes) and, to a lesser extent, in the brain (1 downregulated, rpgrip1l, vs 60 upregulated genes).
source: Filtering the gene list to select for p-adj <0.05 and Log2 FC >0.75 or<–0.75 recovered a vast majority of upregulated genes in the dorsal trunk (75 downregulated vs 614 upregulated genes) and, to a lesser extent, in the brain (1 downregulated, rpgrip1l, vs 60 upregulated genes) as illustrated on the volcano plots from DGE analysis of the brain (Figure 5A) and trunk (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Fifty-four out of 60 genes upregulated in the brain were also upregulated in the trunk, suggesting that, in the trunk, these genes were specific to the CNS.
source: Fifty-four out of 60 genes upregulated in the brain were also upregulated in the trunk, suggesting that, in the trunk, these genes were specific to the CNS (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: In both the brain and the trunk, the most upregulated biological processes in GO term analysis included cilium movement and cilium assembly.
source: In both the brain (Figure 5C) and the trunk (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), the most upregulated biological processes in GO term analysis included cilium movement and cilium assembly.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: The upregulation in both tissues of foxj1a, encoding a master transcriptional activator of genes involved in cilia motility, likely contributed to the enrichment of cilium movement and cilium assembly GO terms.
source: The upregulation in both tissues of foxj1a, encoding a master transcriptional activator of genes involved in cilia motility (Yu et al., 2008; Figure 4E) likely contributed to this enrichment.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the results section based on transcriptomic data and established knowledge.

claim: 106 out of 614 upregulated genes were targets of Foxj1, among which 77 were direct targets.
source: We found that 106 out of 614 upregulated genes were targets of Foxj1, among which 77 were direct targets (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section based on comparison with published datasets.

claim: GO terms enrichment analysis highlighted processes associated with inflammation and innate and adaptive immune responses.
source: Finally, GO terms enrichment analysis also highlighted processes associated with inflammation and innate and adaptive immune responses, as described for the scoliotic ptk7 model (Van Gennip et al., 2018) sharing for example irg1l and complement genes up-regulation (Figure 5C and E, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Quantitative proteomic analysis detected 5706 proteins present in at least 4 over the 5 replicates, of which 172 are associated with a p-value <0.05 and a Log2FC >+0.75 and<–0.75.
source: This analysis detected 5706 proteins present in at least 4 over the 5 replicates, of which 172 are associated with a p-value <0.05 and a Log2FC >+0.75 and<–0.75.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section.

claim: 127 proteins were present in higher and 45 in lower quantity in rpgrip1l-/- brains compared to controls.
source: 127 proteins were present in higher and 45 in lower quantity, as illustrated on the volcano plot (Figure 5F and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Pathways enriched in rpgrip1l-/- brains included regulation of vesicular trafficking and membrane repair processes, as well as proteolysis and catabolic processes.
source: Pathways enriched in rpgrip1l-/- brains included regulation of vesicular trafficking and membrane repair processes, as well as proteolysis and catabolic processes, suggesting profound perturbation of cellular homeostasis (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Several members of the Annexin family were identified among the proteins that were present in highest quantity in mutants: Anxa2a, Anxa1a, Anxa5b.
source: Among the proteins that were present in highest quantity in mutants, several members of the Annexin family were identified: Anxa2a, Anxa1a, Anxa5b (Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Only four proteins (Anxa2a, C4, C7a and Stat3) were the products of genes up-regulated in the transcriptomic study.
source: Of note, only four proteins of that list, Anxa2a, C4, C7a and Stat3, were the products of genes up-regulated in the transcriptomic study.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section based on comparison of transcriptomic and proteomic data.

claim: Immunostaining of brain sections revealed a strong Anxa2 staining on cells lining brain ventricles, such as SCO cells and ventral ependymal cells of the rhombencephalic ventricle (RhV) in rpgrip1l-/- adult fish, which was barely detectable in controls.
source: Immunostaining of brain sections revealed a strong Anxa2 staining on cells lining brain ventricles, such as SCO cells and ventral ependymal cells of the rhombencephalic ventricle (RhV; Figure 6B' and D') in rpgrip1l-/- adult fish, which was barely detectable in controls (Figure 6A' and C'), and to a lesser extent on other brain regions (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A'-F'), suggesting a deregulation of ependymal cell homeostasis.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: In adult rpgrip1l-/- fish, SCO cells were strongly double-positive for Anxa2 and GFAP, while controls displayed much weaker labeling for GFAP in the SCO and no labeling for Anxa2.
source: In adult rpgrip1l-/- fish, SCO cells were strongly double-positive for Anxa2 and GFAP (Figure 6B and B'), while controls displayed much weaker labeling for GFAP in the SCO and no labeling for Anxa2 (Figure 6A and A').
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: The strong increase of GFAP staining combined with Anxa2 overexpression in brain ependymal cells of rpgrip1l-/- adult fish strongly suggests that these cells undergo astrogliosis.
source: Thus, the strong increase of GFAP staining combined with Anxa2 overexpression in brain ependymal cells of rpgrip1l-/- adult fish strongly suggests that these cells undergo astrogliosis as observed in other animal models following CNS injury (Chen et al., 2017; Zamanian et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on immunostaining data and comparison with published literature.

claim: Tail-up juveniles presented a strong GFAP staining in almost all cells of the SCO and along the ventral rhombencephalic ventricle, higher than control levels.
source: Tail-up juveniles (n=3/3) presented a strong GFAP staining in almost all cells of the SCO and along the ventral rhombencephalic ventricle, higher than control levels (Figure 6E, I, H, L and M) while the phenotype of straight fish was heterogeneous: two out of four juveniles presented GFAP-positive cells (Figure 6G and K and red dots on Figure 6M graph), while the two other did not (Figure 6J and green dots on Figure 6M graph) as confirmed by cell quantification (Figure 6M).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Heterogenous GFAP staining among straight mutant fish may support an early role of astrogliosis at SCO and RhV levels in scoliosis onset.
source: As scoliosis onset is asynchronous in rpgrip1l-/-, heterogenous GFAP staining among straight mutant fish may support an early role of astrogliosis at SCO and RhV levels in scoliosis onset.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the results section based on correlation data.

claim: The scoliotic fish presented a higher number of LCP1-positive cells of ameboid shape within SCO cells.
source: We found that the scoliotic fish presented a higher number of LCP1-positive cells of ameboid shape within SCO cells (Figure 6Q, Q' and R).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: The straight mutants that presented a high GFAP staining within SCO cells also showed a higher number of LCP1-positive cells around the SCO than in controls.
source: Strikingly, the straight mutants (2/4) that presented a high GFAP staining within SCO cells (Figure 6G and K) also showed a higher number of LCP1-positive cells around the SCO (Figure 6P and P'; red dots in Figure 6R) than in controls (Figure 6N and N'), while the other straight mutants did not (Figure 6O and O', green dots in Figure 6M) suggesting positive regulation between astrogliosis and macrophages/microglia recruitment.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: In the optic tectum, a twofold increase in the number of ramified LCP1+ cells was observed in straight rpgrip1l-/- juveniles compared to controls.
source: In the optic tectum, where resident LCP1-positive macrophages/microglia were present in controls, a twofold increase in the number of ramified LCP1+ cells was observed in straight rpgrip1l-/- juveniles compared to controls (Figure 6—figure supplement 1H–J).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Scoliotic rpgrip1l-/- fish showed similar LCP1+ cell number as control fish in the tectum.
source: Surprisingly, scoliotic rpgrip1l-/- fish showed similar LCP1+ cell number as control fish in the tectum (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G), suggesting a transient increase of macrophage/microglia activation preceding scoliosis.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: An early astrogliosis process is initiated asynchronously at the SCO and RhV levels of straight rpgrip1l-/- fish, favored by a transient inflammatory state, and preceding the loss of multiciliated tufts around the SCO and that of the RF.
source: Our data thus uncovers an early astrogliosis process initiated asynchronously at the SCO and RhV levels of straight rpgrip1l-/- fish, favored by a transient inflammatory state, and preceding the loss of multiciliated tufts around the SCO and that of the RF, that we only detected in curved rpgrip1l-/- fish.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on correlation data.

claim: Astrogliosis spreads along the brain ventricles and becomes prominent in brain of scoliotic fish.
source: Astrogliosis then spreads along the brain ventricles and becomes prominent in brain of scoliotic fish.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on immunostaining data.

claim: Astrogliosis spread over the whole central nervous system in rpgrip1l mutants.
source: In addition, we found among the upregulated genes in dorsal trunk at scoliosis onset, a number of activated astrocyte markers (Matusova et al., 2023) such as s100b, c4b, gfap, glast/slc1a3b, viml, ctsb, (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), showing that astrogliosis spread over the whole central nervous system.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on transcriptomic data.

claim: 3 mM NACET treatment suppressed the dnaaf1-/- tail-down phenotype.
source: We found that 3 mM NACET treatment suppressed the dnaaf1-/- tail-down phenotype (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–F).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Long-term treatment with 1.5 mM NACET reduced scoliosis penetrance from 92% to 58% and markedly reduced spinal curvature index in rpgrip1l mutants.
source: To suppress scoliosis, we treated the progeny of rpgrip1l+/-incrosses from 4 to 12 wpf with 1.5 mM NACET as in Rose et al., 2020. This long-term treatment reduced scoliosis penetrance from 92% to 58% and markedly reduced spinal curvature index (Figure 7A–C), measured and illustrated as shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1I.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: The intensity and number of GFAP + cells within the SCO were reduced in slightly curved fish and alleviated in straight fish after NACET treatment.
source: Indeed, the intensity and number of GFAP + cells within the SCO were reduced in slightly curved fish and alleviated in straight fish (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: The quantification of Lcp1-positive cells in the SCO region showed a drastic reduction of these cells in NACET-treated fish, back to levels found in rpgrip1l+/+ fish.
source: Furthermore, the quantification of Lcp1-positive cells in the SCO region showed a drastic reduction of these cells in NACET-treated fish, back to levels found in rpgrip1l+/+ fish (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: rpgrip1l-/- juvenile fish display brain astrogliosis and inflammation at scoliosis onset.
source: Our data thus show that rpgrip1l-/- juvenile fish display brain astrogliosis and inflammation at scoliosis onset and that an anti-inflammatory/anti-oxidant treatment of rpgrip1l-/- juveniles is able to maintain a straight axis in approximately one third of the mutants and to slow down curve progression in the other two thirds.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on immunostaining and drug treatment data.

claim: An anti-inflammatory/anti-oxidant treatment of rpgrip1l-/- juveniles is able to maintain a straight axis in approximately one third of the mutants and to slow down curve progression in the other two thirds.
source: Our data thus show that rpgrip1l-/- juvenile fish display brain astrogliosis and inflammation at scoliosis onset and that an anti-inflammatory/anti-oxidant treatment of rpgrip1l-/- juveniles is able to maintain a straight axis in approximately one third of the mutants and to slow down curve progression in the other two thirds.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on drug treatment data.

claim: The beneficial effect of NACET on axis curvature correlates with the combined reduction of astrogliosis and immune cell density.
source: The beneficial effect of NACET on axis curvature correlates with the combined reduction of astrogliosis and immune cell density.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on correlation data.

claim: All cep290fh297/fh297 juveniles developed a fully penetrant scoliosis by 4 wpf.
source: All cep290fh297/fh297 juveniles developed a fully penetrant scoliosis by 4 wpf in our fish facility (n: 30/30).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section.

claim: In cep290-/-, monocilia of the SCO appeared longer than in controls and pointed towards an abnormally elongated diencephalic ventricle.
source: In cep290-/-, monocilia of the SCO appeared longer than in controls (N=3/3) and pointed towards an abnormally elongated diencephalic ventricle (Figure 8D–F).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Fifty percent of SCO cells presented strong GFAP staining in fully scoliotic cep290-/- juveniles, which was not detectable in controls.
source: Fifty percent of SCO cells presented strong GFAP staining in fully scoliotic juveniles, which was not detectable in controls (Figure 8H and K, N=2/3), while a lower proportion (22%) of SCO cells was GFAP positive in the juvenile with a milder curvature (Figure 8M N=1/3).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: A mean of 4 LCP1-positive cells per SCO field was found in cep290-/-, versus 1 in controls.
source: A mean of 4 LCP1-positive cells per SCO field was found in cep290-/-, versus 1 in controls (Figure 8I–L and N).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Both abnormal monocilia, astrogliosis and immune cell enrichment are evidenced at SCO levels in Cep290 -/-.
source: As in rpgrip1l mutants, both abnormal monocilia, astrogliosis and immune cell enrichment are evidenced at SCO levels in Cep290 -/-(3/3).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on immunostaining data.

claim: Astrogliosis was observed within radial glial cells lining the RhV at cerebellar level and at anterior hindbrain level in cep290-/- scoliotic brain.
source: Furthermore, astrogliosis was observed within radial glial cells lining the RhV at cerebellar level (Figure 8P–R) and at anterior hindbrain level (Figure 8T–V), as shown in rpgrip1l-/- scoliotic brain (Figure 6D, K and L).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by figure data.

claim: Astrogliosis is shared by rpgrip1l and cep290 zebrafish scoliotic models.
source: This indicates that astrogliosis is shared by these two zebrafish scoliotic models, even though they develop axis curvature at different stages (3–4 wpf for cep290-/- versus 5–12 wpf for rpgrip1l-/-).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on comparison of immunostaining data.

claim: The full rescue observed after re-introducing RPGRIP1L in foxj1a-expressing cells points towards a crucial function of the protein in cells lining CNS cavities.
source: The full rescue observed after re-introducing RPGRIP1L in foxj1a-expressing cells points towards a crucial function of the protein in cells lining CNS cavities.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on rescue experiment data.

claim: The total loss of multicilia in the fChP of (foxj1b-/-, gmnc-/-) double mutants does not trigger axis curvature.
source: This, combined with the fact that the total loss of multicilia in the fChP of (foxj1b-/-, gmnc-/-) double mutants does not trigger axis curvature (D'Gama et al., 2021) suggests that another foxj1a-expressing population is crucial for axis straightness.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion, supported by a citation.

claim: Cilia defects in the SCO trigger axis curvature in rpgrip1l mutants.
source: Our results strongly suggest that cilia defects in the SCO trigger axis curvature in rpgrip1l mutants.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on correlation data.

claim: Most ciliary mutant models develop axis curvature at 3–4 weeks, a stage when brain multiciliated cells are not yet differentiated.
source: This is consistent with the literature showing that most ciliary mutant models develop axis curvature at 3–4 weeks, a stage when brain multiciliated cells are not yet differentiated (D'Gama et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion, supported by a citation.

claim: sspo-/- hypomorphic mutants which present aggregates within ventricles have been shown to present an inflammatory response.
source: However, as sspo-/- hypomorphic mutants which present aggregates within ventricles have been shown to present an inflammatory response (Rose et al., 2020), it is equally possible that SCO astrogliosis is a downstream consequence of the presence of these proteoglycans aggregates in contact with primary cilia or ventricular cell surfaces (Supplementary file 5 - Graphical abstract, green arrow).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion, supported by a citation.

claim: Forced expression of urp1/2 induces a tail-up phenotype in embryos and juveniles.
source: As forced expression of urp1/2 induces a tail-up phenotype in embryos and juveniles (Zhang et al., 2018; Gaillard et al., 2023; Lu et al., 2020), we attempted to rescue rpgrip1l-/- axis curvature by down-regulating urp1/2 expression.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion, supported by citations.

claim: Increased urp1/2 expression level does not significantly contribute to axis curvature in rpgrip1l-/- fish.
source: No beneficial effect on scoliosis penetrance or severity was observed, indicating that increased urp1/2 expression level does not significantly contribute to axis curvature in rpgrip1l-/- fish.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on genetic interaction data.

claim: In zebrafish, radial glial cells are endowed with both neurogenic and astrocytic functions, and are thus also called astroglial cells.
source: In zebrafish, radial glial cells are endowed with both neurogenic and astrocytic functions, and are thus also called astroglial cells (Jurisch-Yaksi et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion, supported by a citation.

claim: In two murine models of primary ciliary dyskinesia, decreased CSF flow was associated with gliosis at juvenile stage.
source: In two murine models of primary ciliary dyskinesia, decreased CSF flow was associated with gliosis at juvenile stage (Finn et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion, supported by a citation.

claim: foxj1a expression is upregulated in the CNS of three other scoliotic models in addition to rpgrip1l, namely in ptk7, sspo and katnb1 mutants.
source: foxj1a expression is also reported to be upregulated in the CNS of three other scoliotic models in addition to rpgrip1l, namely in ptk7, sspo and katnb1 mutants (Escartin et al., 2021; Meyer-Miner et al., 2022; Van Gennip et al., 2018), suggesting that it constitutes a common response to similar ventricular and CSF defects.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion, supported by citations.

claim: foxj1a expression is upregulated upon zebrafish embryonic or adult spinal cord injury.
source: Interestingly, foxj1a expression is also upregulated upon zebrafish embryonic (Cavone et al., 2021; Hellman et al., 2010) or adult (Ribeiro et al., 2017) spinal cord injury.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion, supported by citations.

claim: In several neurodegenerative murine animal models, GSK3b enzymatic activity was shown to promote inflammation and gliosis.
source: In several neurodegenerative murine animal models, GSK3b enzymatic activity was shown to promote inflammation and gliosis (Jorge-Torres et al., 2018; Medina and Avila, 2010; Mines et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion, supported by citations.

claim: Impaired mitochondrial activity within ciliated astrocytes leads to the induction of the Foxj1 ciliary motility program, the elongation and distortion of astrocyte primary cilia as well as reactive astrogliosis.
source: We think this is of particular interest in light of a recent report demonstrating that impaired mitochondrial activity within ciliated astrocytes leads to the induction of the Foxj1 ciliary motility program, the elongation and distortion of astrocyte primary cilia as well as reactive astrogliosis (Ignatenko et al., 2023), three phenotypes also observed in rpgrip1l-/- brains.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion, supported by a citation.

claim: Astrogliosis markers such as glast/slc1a3b, vim, s100b, c4, timp2b, gfap and ctssb.2, are upregulated in the transcriptome of ptk7 mutants.
source: Of note, astrogliosis markers such as glast/slc1a3b, vim, s100b, c4, timp2b, gfap and ctssb.2, are also upregulated in the transcriptome of ptk7 mutants (Van Gennip et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion, supported by a citation.

claim: Sustained astrogliosis might impair neuronal survival and activity, crucial for proper interoception and locomotor control, thus leading to axis curvature in the context of a rapidly growing axial skeleton.
source: We propose that sustained astrogliosis might impair neuronal survival and activity, crucial for proper interoception and locomotor control, thus leading to axis curvature in the context of a rapidly growing axial skeleton.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion stated in the discussion.

claim: A similar context of astrocytosis associated with spinal cord dilation has been observed in human patients with syringomyelia.
source: A similar context of astrocytosis associated with spinal cord dilation has been observed in human patients with syringomyelia.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion.

claim: The population with syringomyelia has a high incidence of scoliosis and can present hyper-signals on T2 MRI scans, which were proposed to reflect local astrocytosis.
source: This population with a high incidence of scoliosis can present hyper-signals on T2 MRI scans, which were proposed to reflect local astrocytosis and could be validated by biopsies in rare cases (Sherman et al., 1987).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion, supported by a citation.
